title: dawn4k public contract inventory
purpose: Manual review support: every member of the RESOLVED WebGPU API snapshot (the webgpu-api and webgpu-descriptors sources jars actually resolved by the build) appears exactly once below, with the dawn4k implementation, the native symbol it reaches, the functional tests that cover it, and the limitations. This file is NOT a build input: no automated coverage test or gate consumes it, and it deliberately reflects the resolved snapshot (not a master clone).

nativeSide.bindings: org.graphiks.dawn4k.native (generated by kextract from the Dawn release pinned in bindings/dawn.lock.json)

legends.implementationFiles: Keys are paths under dawn4k/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/graphiks/dawn4k/ unless a full path is given. Test classes are the @Test classes of dawn4k/src/commonTest/kotlin/org/graphiks/dawn4k/. testIds are 'Class.method'. GPU test classes run only through the gpuTest* tasks; the pure classes run through the standard test tasks.

entryShape.symbol: the snapshot member, qualified by its declaring type
entryShape.kind: interface | mixin | property | function | enum | bitflag | typealias | dataClass | artifactMember
entryShape.implementationFile: where dawn4k implements or consumes the member (array; empty means the artifact provides it and dawn4k never touches it)
entryShape.nativeSymbol: the native entity the member reaches (array; empty means no native counterpart — Kotlin-side metadata or marker)
entryShape.testIds: functional tests covering the member (array; empty = no direct test, see limitations)
entryShape.limitations: honest notes, holes and deliberate behaviours

interfaces.limitations: Sealed in webgpu-api. The backend's buffer/sampler/texture/texture-view wrappers implement it directly; the descriptors module's BufferBinding data class is the other leaf used by bind-group entries. A Kotlin-only marker: no native counterpart (each resource carries its own handle type).

Mapping is real (a borrowed view, never a CPU copy): getMappedRange's ArrayBuffer is invalid after unmap/close and this is NOT guarded — never dereference it after invalidation. Single-threaded object model: map/unmap/close must not race one another. close() destroys (tombstone until teardown) so the native handle stays valid for late native errors.
